clue.text: Do take legal action 'about' females in charge

indicators.note: the quoted 'about' tells us one piece goes round the others

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Women in authority are being taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the definition, as in 'that will do'; the quote marks round 'about' show it is the container signal, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to be enough or adequate for a purpose.

clue.text: Announced opportunity for bargain cruise

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a sale is an event offering bargains

explanation.surface: A cut-price holiday at sea is advertised.
explanation.definitionFit: To cruise is to travel by ship, a synonym of the verb sail.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about head's subtlety

indicators.note: about means placed round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone makes a rude noise about the boss's clever touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the boss but a geographical headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill or refinement, a synonym of subtlety.

clue.text: Fish on a lake — perfect

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A fish swimming on a lake is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so IDE sits over A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, the same as perfect.

clue.text: Power of the interpretive artist

definitions.meaning: in mathematics an index or power such as the 2 in x squared
a performer who expounds or interprets a work, such as a pianist

explanation.definitionFit: In maths an index is called this, and a performer who interprets music or a doctrine is also so called.

clue.text: Unusually nice gal, of beautiful disposition

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: An exceptionally pleasant young woman with a lovely nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly, sweet-natured people are likened to heavenly beings, so the word describes a lovely temperament.

clue.text: It supports us comfortably during periods of inflation

definitions.text: It supports us comfortably during periods of inflation

parts.words: It supports us comfortably during periods of inflation
parts.note: reads like economics about rising prices, but describes a mattress that is blown up and slept on

explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress holds a sleeper only while it is pumped full of air.

clue.text: Two chaps making headgear in Scotland

parts.note: Glen is a man's name
Garry is another man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men are producing hats north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The two chaps are two first names joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a brimless Scottish cap, a kind of military bonnet.

clue.text: Method of restarting play or sketch, exchanging parts

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places, front going to the back

parts.note: an outline is a rough sketch

explanation.surface: Choosing between restarting a game and a drawing in which parts are swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging parts' swaps OUT and LINE. In rugby a lineout restarts play after the ball goes into touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the ball is thrown in between two lines of players to resume the game after it leaves the field.

clue.text: A primate employs him in peace movement around New Zealand

indicators.note: him is to be placed inside the rest of the wordplay
the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
movement signals the letters of the word peace are shifted about

explanation.surface: An ape hires a man to campaign for peace in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peace movement' looks like a campaign group, but 'movement' is the anagram signal; NZ goes inside the shuffled letters ('around') and the man is put 'in' after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is an African great ape, one of the primates.

clue.text: Accommodating person wearing new ring

parts.note: if you are in a garment you are wearing it
a keeper is a ring worn to hold another ring in place

explanation.surface: Someone obliging is putting on a new ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodating' means providing lodgings, not being obliging.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord of a pub or tavern provides rooms for travellers to stay in.

clue.text: Lack of interest English university revealed in withdrawing 9's place

indicators.note: the letter is shown sitting inside the other piece
withdrawing means retreating, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 9 across keeps an inn

explanation.surface: An English academic shows no interest as he leaves the landlord's pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns the innkeeper's place backwards; 9 refers to the answer at 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a feeling of having no interest in anything.

clue.text: Dissenters stopping ruler: implementing new order

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Rebels halt a dictator who is imposing a new regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction that breaks away from a larger body because its members disagree.

clue.text: Timely when son replaces fair beginner

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: reasonable means fair or just

explanation.surface: A good moment arrives when a boy takes over from a novice at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginner' points to the first letter, R, of REASONABLE, which S 'replaces'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seasonable comes at the right time or suits the season, so it is opportune.

clue.text: Meat 1 dropped; say, outside office in church

indicators.note: the two letters go on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

indicators.note: dropped means a letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: venison is deer meat
the numeral one looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: With one meat dish cancelled, a church office is held outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from VENISON leaving VENSON, which E and G go 'outside'. An office here is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Anglican church, one of its daily offices.

clue.text: Fellow illustrator — one working on docks

parts.note: Steve is a man's name, so a fellow
Gustave Dore was a famous French book illustrator

explanation.surface: A colleague who draws pictures works at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a docker who loads and unloads ships.

clue.text: Sombre tones from a Frenchman? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Frenchman speaks in a gloomy voice, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' reverses the sentence: a Frenchman comes 'from' the words 'Sombre tones', where he is spelt out across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a native of Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Five in vehicle detained in African scrubland

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: in means the numeral is put inside the other word

parts.note: held means detained
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five people are kept on a bus in the African bush.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes 'in' HELD after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushveld is the area of South Africa covered by scrub and low trees.

clue.text: Subdue back of class at frequent intervals

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: often means many times over

explanation.surface: Calm down the pupils at the back, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something is to make it milder or tone it down.

clue.text: It helps one when driving, having arranged golf with a member

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A golfer books a round with a politician and drives over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges GOLF to FOGL. 'driving' hints at golf, but means motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright car lamp used in fog lets a motorist see the road in poor visibility.

clue.text: Important-sounding team in 14's workplace

indicators.note: the hyphen ties 'sounding' to the word before, so that word is heard rather than written

parts.note: key means important or vital
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An impressive team at the docker's place of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 is the stevedore of 14 down, so the definition points to the docker's place of work; only 'Important' is affected by '-sounding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads ships at the wharf or harbour edge.

clue.text: Fire in part of church

parts.note: a spire is the pointed tower of a church

explanation.surface: Blaze in a church steeple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' is the verb, as in fire someone with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire people up is to stir and motivate them.

clue.text: Founder of gallery sailing for America

annotationWithheld.why: Founder of gallery sailing for America (6): TATE inside SS, but 'sailing' has to give both the ship SS and the instruction to put TATE inside it, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Founder of gallery sailing for America

clue.text: Fairly insignificant evidence of a mild attack of ague.

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something not very good or important

definitions.text: evidence of a mild attack of ague.
definitions.meaning: read literally, a bout of fever with only slight shivering

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mediocre, while a mild fever literally produces only small tremors.

clue.text: This country is upset over party's prestige

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: the UK is the setter's home country
a do is a party, with the S from the possessive

explanation.surface: The nation is annoyed by a party's high standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is honour or acclaim, the same as prestige.

clue.text: Without qualifications, even

definitions.meaning: as in a ... refusal, absolute with no conditions

explanation.definitionFit: The word means absolute, as in a downright refusal, and also level or smooth.

clue.text: Algonquian warrior cut down by old assassin

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: brave was the old term for a Native American warrior

explanation.surface: A Native American fighter is killed by a veteran hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' drops the last letter E from BRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is a hired thug or killer, an old word from Italian.

clue.text: Prisoners took steps once to promote its revolution

definitions.text: Prisoners took steps once to promote its revolution

parts.words: Prisoners took steps once to promote its revolution
parts.note: reads like a prison uprising, but describes inmates of old treading a wheel to turn it

explanation.definitionFit: Victorian convicts walked on the steps of a large wheel, turning it as punishment.

clue.text: Rapidly dispatch couch

definitions.meaning: to send something by fast delivery
to put into words, as in couched in polite terms

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to send fast and also to phrase or put into words.

clue.text: A fool, perhaps, having locks sent back

indicators.note: sent back signals the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tressed means having tresses, locks of hair

explanation.surface: An idiot with long hair is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a fruit pudding, not an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a pudding of fruit and cream, so an example of a sweet course.
